body: deferred-verdict-check-counts-only-open-issues: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:unfiled_deferred (L2224-2234) builds its texts from issues.select(root), and plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/issues:select (L684-697) reads only live records unless state_is='closed', so an issue the next /plan-sprint promotes (moved to .ok-planner/history/issues.jsonl, closed_as promoted) no longer counts; review:suite_failures (L2203-2206) then returns 'fails' for item 3. The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: review certified --sprint checks first whether the sprint is archived with a closed: stamp, which is terminal and skips this check, so the trigger is a certified rerun of a sprint that is not yet archived after the next /plan-sprint promoted the deferred verdict's issue; certify-completion's verdict would flip from SPRINT COMPLETE to not complete with nothing in the sprint changed. Corpus: story:certify-completion 'so that done means the same thing for every sprint' (leans toward a verdict later intake work cannot flip); decision:product-slow-fixes-ride-a-round-that-runs-anyway 'each product-slow verdict still standing goes to the intake as a judgment issue for the next sprint' (silent on whether promotion still counts as the record); the owner-list prompt (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/owner-list.md) dedupes against an open issue at the same site. Harm: A9 shape (a false not-complete report) in the rerun window only. Options: A. count only open issues, as built: simplest, matches the owner list's dedupe, costs a false failure on a rerun after the next sprint promotes the issue; B. count open issues and archived issues closed as promoted: the verdict stays stable across the next /plan-sprint, costs a select over the archive and a choice of which close states count; C. (filer missed) count any intake record, open or archived in any close state, that names the site: never flips, but an issue retired or answered without a fix would also satisfy the check. Recommend B: promotion is the intended end of a deferred verdict's issue per the decision's 'for the next sprint', and the story wants a stable done; flip to A if certified is never rerun before archiving. No code change touches .ok-planner/design/. Sibling: review-facts-omit-deferred-verdict-check (retired in this pass; facts-file wording for the same check).

plan-sprint-sign-off-rereads-whole-scope-every-round: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md section 7 Sign-off (L193-199) still dispatches one compliance reviewer (skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md, draft mode) over every corpus, docspec, and surface intent delta and every live file they amend, fixes findings, and says 'Re-dispatch until a round raises no unsettled finding'; [SETTLED] carries prior findings, but each round rereads the whole scope. The filed facts (nine rounds over 46 deltas in the eighth intake-drain sprint; owner stopped after round 9) are history and not re-checkable from the tree, but the text that produces them stands. Mechanism: one reader per round samples part of a large scope, and each fix adds text the next round reads, so rounds keep finding old defects and new ones in fixed text and do not converge. Tooling the change edits: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md section 7, likely skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md (lens split, fix-only verification), and the materialized copies true-up writes from them. Corpus: no live decision fixes sign-off's shape; decision:converge-finds-then-fixes and decision:analysis-hunts-until-converged record the find-then-fix and hunt-until-converged shape for /converge with its rationale ('A loop that re-read every file a fix touched found something new in each round ... so it ran to its cap'), which argues for A by analogy but does not bind /plan-sprint; story:plan-a-sprint promises a signed-off, self-sufficient sprint. SKILL.md section 7 also says 'This review is the only point at which a delta's claims are checked for truth', so any option must keep full coverage of every delta. Harm: owner time and session cost; no accept-list entry needed (judgment issue on tooling). Options: A. /converge shape (several single-lens readers per delta cluster, hunt until a hunt adds few findings, one merge, one fix pass, verifiers read only fixed passages): converges and finds most defects before fixing, costs more dispatches up front and a new cluster/lens structure in the skill and reviewer file, and a fix-only verifier can miss a fix's effect on an unchanged delta; B. one reader per round, later rounds read only changed deltas plus deltas that cite them: smallest edit, but round 1 still reads past defects in a large scope and the later rounds never reread them; C. keep as is: no change, costs non-converging rounds on large sprints; D. (filer missed) partition the full scope across several readers per round, each over a cluster small enough to read whole, keeping the rerun-until-clean rule: better first-round coverage than C at modest cost, but still rereads every cluster each round. A decision artifact recording the chosen shape would be a corpus delta in the promoting sprint. Recommend A, flip to D if dispatch cost per sprint matters more than round count. Siblings: none open.

body: short-close-frees-waiting-tasks: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:open_waits (L807-813) counts a wait satisfied once the waited-on task's state is CLOSED, whatever its outcome; ready (L816) is its negation. Sprint execution's shared text (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:472-474) refiles a partial close for its remainder with tasks refile and a blocked close once, but only after the drain reports back; the drain loop (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_tasks/drain.md:250) 'Does not judge an outcome' and moves to the next task, so a waiter is issued before the refile lands. tasks:cmd_refile (L1060-1085) adds the refile to the after list of each waiter still open, which misses a waiter already claimed. The filed facts hold. Mechanism: a short close frees its waiters at once; a refile wires only waiters still open. Corpus: concept:task-tracker says the tracker 'decides nothing and judges nothing'; decision:team-execution-cold-gate: 'Code complete means every task of every build stage closed done at its latest filing: a task that closed blocked and was filed again counts by its refile'; decision:stopped-run-resumes runs again every task not closed done; /converge's fix chains regroup a partial fixer and its drive relays never refile a blocked driver (converge/SKILL.md step 6), so both rely on the current rule. No artifact says whether a short close holds its waiters. Harm: a waiting build stage builds on an unfinished stage (three times in the eighth intake-drain sprint, each claim within 11 seconds of the partial close); no accept-list entry decides which rule is right, and a /converge fixer's decline of it as a defect was verified for that reason. Options: A, satisfy a wait only on done or on a refiled task, with an explicit release for /converge's chains and relays: changes the tracker, both /converge loops, and how a stopped run's record reads; B, hold the waiters of a short close only for roles a run names, set by sprint execution for its build stages: a new tracker setting and a sprint template change, /converge untouched; C, keep the tracker, and commit sprint execution to refile a short build stage, or hold the drain, before the next claim: no tracker change, but the drain loop then judges an outcome, which drain.md:250 rules out today, so the drain loop changes too. Siblings: none in this batch.

decisions-bundling-several-choices-await-a-split: Evidence, re-verified: the four decisions still bundle as filed. .ok-planner/design/decisions/team-execution-cold-gate.md (233 lines) holds sprint execution as build tasks, code complete by latest filing, the claim order (the task most tasks wait on), and the fork protocol; tests-isolated-unless-declared.md (153 lines) the schedule forms, run locks, and ranking bound; test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests.md (166 lines) the flaky-test route, run-alone rerun, and silence stop; drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user.md (116 lines) the driver per story, variants, public surface with a local stand-in, scratch copy, skill-surface review, and confirm drive. Code citations: tests-isolated-unless-declared, test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests, and drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user are cited by @decision: in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests and scripts/review; team-execution-cold-gate has no code citation, and six corpus files reference it by 'see also'. Filed option B (keep the bundles) breaks the definition rule; it would change that rule, not choose within it. Harm: a later change to one choice rewrites the others' rationale, and a reader cannot cite one choice alone. Recommendation: generated. Siblings: none in this batch.

setup-web-headless-server: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok-web/skills/setup-web/SKILL.md (ok-web v31.0.0, owned by this repository) step 3 writes one entry, mcpServers.chrome-devtools, args ["-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest", "--userDataDir=${HOME}/.cache/chrome-devtools-mcp/profiles/<project-name>"]; it names no headless entry, and its merge rules cover only the chrome-devtools key. Step 5's report says two concurrent sessions in the same project share that project's profile and only one can hold the browser at a time, a limit an --isolated headless server removes. The skill's opening says new web-project MCPs are added here 'each under the same merge-never-clobber discipline'. Corpus: no concept, story, or decision covers setup-web or the browser tooling; .ok-planner/surface/surface.md:31 makes plugins/ok-web/skills/*/SKILL.md public slash commands, so a new entry changes a public command's output. The filer's verantel entry also carries --chrome-arg=--host-resolver-rules=MAP *.test 127.0.0.1, a project-specific mapping a generic entry should not carry. Options: A, write both entries by default (chrome-devtools headed; chrome-devtools-headless with --headless --isolated) under the same merge rules, the report saying when to use each: every project gets a second server to approve and load; B, write the headless entry only on an argument such as /setup-web --headless: the skill takes its first argument, and a project must know to ask; C, stay headed-only, with the report naming how to add a headless entry by hand: no new write, and same-project contention stays. The ruling also fixes the flag set: --headless --isolated alone, leaving host-resolver rules to each project. The owner's stated want (both) favors A. Siblings: none.

preflight-setup-checks-with-no-recorded-test: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-preflight.md check 6 (L47-53) ends 'Where the scenario list records no test, check only that each setup run exits 0', and check 7 (L54-62) 'Where the scenario list records no test, check only that setup exits 0 and the scratch resource still stands'. /ok-setup's runner check (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-setup/SKILL.md:127, step 3.7) reads 'Where the scenario list records no test, say so in one line, and end the step', so it runs none of its three checks. The filed facts hold. Mechanism: both checks prove the stack ready by passing a recorded test; with none recorded, the preflight keeps the exit and resource-survival halves, and /ok-setup drops all three checks. A project's first tested sprint meets this case, since its preflight runs before its first test task records a test. Corpus: decision:suite-contracts-checked-before-a-round says the preflight and the runner check 'each run three checks of the project's suite run, wherever each of them runs', including that setup 'readies the stack and leaves those resources standing'; it is silent on a project with no recorded test, and today the two sites differ. Harm: none an accept-list entry names; a setup fault the partial check would catch otherwise costs a whole-suite round (the decision's rationale). Options: A, the preflight checks setup's exit and the survival of resources it did not create with no recorded test, as built: keeps the cheap checks, and /ok-setup stays different; B, the preflight skips checks 6 and 7 whole with no recorded test, as /ok-setup does: the two agree, and a fresh project's first sprint meets setup faults in a whole-suite round; C, missed by the filer, both the preflight and /ok-setup's runner check run the exit and resource-survival halves with no recorded test: the two agree and a fresh project keeps the cheap checks, at the cost of an /ok-setup change. Recommended: C, or A where the owner wants /ok-setup left as it stands. Siblings: none.

Options: A, write both entries by default (chrome-devtools headed; chrome-devtools-headless with --headless --isolated) under the same merge rules, the report saying when to use each: every project gets a second server to approve and load; B, write the headless entry only on an argument such as /setup-web --headless: the skill takes its first argument, and a project must know to ask; C, stay headed-only, with the report naming how to add a headless entry by hand: no new write, and same-project contention stays. - i18: preflight-setup-checks-with-no-recorded-test: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-preflight.md check 6 (L47-53) ends 'Where the scenario list records no test, check only that each setup run exits 0', and check 7 (L54-62) 'Where the scenario list records no test, check only that setup exits 0 and the scratch resource still stands'. /ok-setup's runner check (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-setup/SKILL.md:127, step 3.7) reads 'Where the scenario list records no test, say so in one line, and end the step', so it runs none of its three checks. The filed facts hold. Mechanism: both checks prove the stack ready by passing a recorded test; with none recorded, the preflight keeps the exit and resource-survival halves, and /ok-setup drops all three checks. A project's first tested sprint meets this case, since its preflight runs before its first test task records a test. Corpus: decision:suite-contracts-checked-before-a-round says the preflight and the runner check 'each run three checks of the project's suite run, wherever each of them runs', including that setup 'readies the stack and leaves those resources standing'; it is silent on a project with no recorded test, and today the two sites differ. Harm: none an accept-list entry names; a setup fault the partial check would catch otherwise costs a whole-suite round (the decision's rationale). Options: A, the preflight checks setup's exit and the survival of resources it did not create with no recorded test, as built: keeps the cheap checks, and /ok-setup stays different; B, the preflight skips checks 6 and 7 whole with no recorded test, as /ok-setup does: the two agree, and a fresh project's first sprint meets setup faults in a whole-suite round; C, missed by the filer, both the preflight and /ok-setup's runner check run the exit and resource-survival halves with no recorded test: the two agree and a fresh project keeps the cheap checks, at the cost of an /ok-setup change. Recommended: C, or A where the owner wants /ok-setup left as it stands. Siblings: none.
